videos.title: Eight-deck shuffle
videos.note: 八副牌洗牌：对半、右边转 180 度，抓 1 到 1.5 副，riffle riffle strip riffle。考核目标三分半。
videos.transcript_note: 逐字稿来自录音。切牌卡、eight-deck shuffle 已按第二遍听写核对。考核时间原文是 by audition time。有一句讲为什么转 180 度，教室里比较糊，英文按听写保留。
videos.transcript_en: You're going to put all eight decks where it says pays, or right around in that area. Now what you need to do is you need to cut the deck in half. It doesn't have to be exact, but it has to be close. A good way to also do that is you can just break it down and put it right next to it. See, it's pretty much level. Now once we cut the deck in half, this is very important. We are going to rotate the deck on the right-hand side. 180 degrees, with your finger, and it's always going to be on the right side. You just do it with your finger, 180 degrees. One important reason, probably what you'd understand right now, is because we don't keep the shuffle in the same corners all the time. Now, once we have it cut into two even piles and he rotates 180, at the same time he's going to go and grab cards. Ideally you want between a deck and a deck and a half of cards. You don't put them together. This right here is probably close to a deck and a half, maybe a deck and a quarter. This is pretty good. You don't want a lot of cards, because if you have more than this, when you riffle it's going to jam up and it's going to be hard. Anything less, like if you do like this, you'll be shuffling forever. So remember, ideally it's between a deck and a deck and a half. Now you're going to put the cards together, and now you're pulling them apart. And now you're going to do what you already know: riffle, riffle, strip, riffle. This is your second riffle. Now strip: one, two, three, and on top, and then riffle. Then you put the cards onto the cut card in the middle. Now you're going to grab cards from both the middle and the end. We have a little bit more from here than here, just a little bit more. Put the cards together, then pull them apart, and then you're going to alternate side to side until we get into one pile. Ideally you want to get this done in less than three and a half minutes. Now that's by audition time, okay? I had a gentleman. He was like in his older 60s. He came in part time. But his first shuffle was like 16 minutes and 47 seconds. By the end of the four weeks, his shuffle was done in like 3 minutes and 27 seconds. So don't get overwhelmed. They'll get there, trust me. Now that you guys know this eight-deck shuffle, when you first get to this class every single day, you don't have to look for me for what to do. You punch in, and you automatically go to a table and do your eight-deck shuffle. Everyone's got to do one eight-deck shuffle when they get to class, and then we start the day after that. And here's his last part: riffle, riffle, strip, riffle. Okay, any questions?
videos.transcript_zh: 把八副牌放在毡上写着 pays 的地方，或者就在那一块附近。现在要把这叠牌对半切开。不必刚好一半，但要接近。也可以拆开并排摆。看，两边基本上一样高。对半切开之后，这一步很重要。我们要转右边那一叠。用手指转 180 度，而且永远转右边那一叠。就用手指转 180 度。一个现在就能懂的原因是：不要让洗牌总停在同样的几个角上。（这句教室里有点糊，英文按听写保留）切成两叠、转了 180 度之后，同时去抓牌。最好抓一副到一副半。先不要把它们合在一起。这里大概接近一副半，也许一副又四分之一。这样挺好。牌不要太多。再多，riffle 的时候会卡住，很难洗拢。抓得太少，你会洗个没完。所以记住，最好是一副到一副半。现在把牌合上，再拉开。然后做你已经会的：riffle，riffle，strip，riffle。这是第二次 riffle。然后 strip：一、二、三，放到上面，再 riffle。然后把牌放到中间的切牌卡上。接下来从中间和两端都抓牌。这边比那边多抓一点点，就多一点点。合上，拉开，左右交替，直到合成一叠。最好在三分半以内做完。这是考核时的时间，好吗？我有过一个学员，六十多岁。他是兼职来的。他第一次洗牌大约 16 分 47 秒。四周课结束时，他大约 3 分 27 秒就能洗完。所以别被吓到。他们做得到的，相信我。你们会了这个八副洗牌。以后每天一到课，不用找我问该干什么。打卡之后，自己去一张桌，做八副牌洗牌。到课先做一次八副洗牌，然后再开始当天的课。最后再看一遍：riffle，riffle，strip，riffle。还有问题吗？

videos.transcript_en: Let's talk about splits. A split is when we take one hand and split it into two complete separate hands. We have a couple of rules. The first rule is you can only split for the same amount. If Steve's got a twenty-dollar bet, it's got to be twenty dollars to split. It can't be less, and it can't be more. The cards have to be the same point value. A two and a two we can split, because they're both worth two. If we have a seven and a two, can we split that? No. It has to be the same point value. Can we split these two? Yes, because they're both worth ten. These two? Yes, because they're all worth ten points. It's based on your point value. They have to be the same point value. When we split, two things are your responsibility as a dealer. The first thing you've got to do is get a signal. A signal for a split is this, with your two fingers. You need to get that. Here's why. We have options. He could double, or he could split. We need to know what he's doing. If he doesn't give you a signal, ask him: Sir, what would you like to do? Every time someone splits, you have to make sure the new bet is on the right-hand side. That's the first thing. If he puts the bet right there, you're all set. Most players who have played a long time will set it on that side, because they know. Every once in a while you get a guest who doesn't know, or someone doing it on purpose. Just put it on that side. First thing: hand signal. Second thing: make sure the bet is on the right-hand side. The last thing you need to do is prove the bet. Even if it's one cheque, you've got to prove the bet. We're not doing it for us. Who are we doing it for? The camera. Prove the bet. Then make it look like a split. Give it a little separation. They're not friends anymore. The original card goes with the original bet. This card goes with this bet, and this card goes with this bet. Now we have two separate hands. They don't have anything to do with each other anymore. We can split for a total of four hands, which means we split three times. If he wants to split again, we can do that. We can split up to four times. Bring the new bet all the way to the right. You don't have to size this one against a different amount, because they all have to be the same. Original card, second card, prove the bet, make it look like a split, and bring the new card around. If the hand loses, casinos are greedy. Take the money first. Where does it go? Top of the rack. Then lock up the hand. If he wants to split, get the signal, prove it, and move the cards so you have room. We cannot overlap cards. It's very taboo. You can't do it. On your first two cards, you have to see the pips. After that, if the hands get tight, you have a little leeway. As long as it's readable and you're not overlapping cards, you're okay. If you cover a pip because a lot is going on, that's okay later. Just on the first two cards, you want to see the pips. Once you start splitting several hands, and people are playing on both sides, it's going to get tight. Use common sense and make it work. Don't just cover pips on the first two cards.
videos.transcript_zh: 这节讲分牌。分牌就是把一手分成完全独立的两手。有几条必须遵守。第一条：只能下同样的金额。Steve 原来是 20 块，分牌也必须是 20 块。不能少，也不能多。两张牌必须点数相同。两张 2 可以分，都是 2 点。7 和 2 能不能分？不能。必须点数相同。这两张呢？可以，因为都是 10 点。另外两张也可以，因为 10 点的牌都是 10 点。看的是点数，不是花色。分牌时有两件事是荷官的责任。第一件是拿到手势。分牌的手势是两根手指，做成 V。一定要看到。因为客人还有选择，他可以加倍，也可以分牌。你得知道他要哪一个。他不给手势，你就问：Sir, what would you like to do? 每次有人分牌，新注必须在右侧。这是第一步。他如果已经放在那边，就对了。玩得久的客人通常会自己放对。偶尔会遇到不会玩的，或者故意放错的。你就把它放到右侧。顺序是：先手势，再确认注在右侧，最后证明这笔注。哪怕只有一张筹码，也要证明。不是做给我们自己看。做给谁？给摄像机。证明完，再做成一副分牌的样子。两手分开一点。它们不再是一手了。原来的牌跟着原来的注。这张跟这笔，那张跟那笔。现在是两手完全分开的牌，彼此没关系了。一共可以有 4 手，也就是分 3 次。他还想再分，可以。后面他随口说了 up to four times。这句和刚说的 three times 不一致，也和讲义不一致。记讲义：最多分 3 次，一共 4 手。新注一路放到右边。金额必须一样，所以不用拿不同的数目去 size。原牌、第二张、证明注、分成两手的样子，再把新牌转过来。这手输了，赌场要先拿钱。钱放哪？筹码槽的最上面。然后把这手锁上，继续走。客人要分，先看手势，证明注，牌分开，留出地方。牌不能重叠。这是禁忌。前两张必须看见所有 pips。后面如果台面挤，可以通融一点。只要看得清、不重叠，就行。后面因为东西多，盖住一个 pip，可以。只有前两张，pips 都要露出来。分的手一多，两边都有客人，就会挤。要有常识，把牌摆得能看。不要一上来就把前两张的 pips 盖住。

videos.transcript_en: I'll preface with this. Turning Stone allows players to double down on any first two cards, and you get only one card. Yes, that's a really good explanation. A double down means you can double your bet, but the trade-off is you only get one card. When I say up to the original bet, that means you can double down for less. Can he double down for more? No. Absolutely not. Same thing as splits. What was the first thing with splits? We need to see a signal. Why? Because he had choices. The only stipulation on a double down is that you have to double down on your first two cards. It doesn't matter what you have, as long as it's not 21. He puts the money down. Does he need to give you a signal? Is there a signal for doubling down? Technically there is. But if he sets his money down right now, can he split that? No, he can't split that, so he doesn't have any choices. Him putting his money down, that's his signal. Over on the pair, he could split or he could double down, so he's got choices. You need signals when you have choices. Over here there is no choice, so if he puts his money down, that's his signal. Nothing else changes. The new bet has got to go to the right. And the last thing we have to do is prove the bet. That's doubling down. You can double your bet, but you only get one card. Another thing people might do is add the money on top of their original bet. You have to be aware of your game. Now over here is a 12. Can you double on that? Yes, he can. Move it to the right side. We need to prove the bet. Just setting it down is not proving the bet. You size into it and prove it. Is doubling a hard 12 a smart thing to do? Statistically, no, because he has a chance of breaking and losing the money. Just like when we shuffle, you have to announce it. Just like when the yellow card comes out, what do we say? Last hand. You're not getting permission. You're announcing it loud. This is what we call a red flag, because he has a chance of breaking.
videos.transcript_zh: 我先说在前面。Turning Stone 允许客人用任意前两张加倍，而且只给一张牌。这个解释很好。加倍就是可以把注加倍，换来的是只拿一张牌。我说到原注为止，意思是可以 double down for less，少于原注。可以多于原注吗？不行。绝对不行。这和分牌一样。分牌第一件事是什么？要看到手势。为什么？因为他还有选择。加倍只有一条限制：必须在前两张上加倍。只要不是 21，是什么牌都可以。他把钱放下了。还要手势吗？加倍有没有手势？严格说有。可是他现在把钱放下，这手还能分牌吗？不能。所以他没有别的选择。他把钱放下，这本身就是信号。那边如果是对子，既可以分也可以加倍，他有选择。有选择的时候才要手势。这边没有选择，钱放下就是信号。别的不变。新注要放到右边。最后一件事是证明这笔注。这就是加倍。你可以加倍，但只拿一张牌。有的客人会把钱叠在原注上面。你得看住自己的桌。这边是 12。这手能加倍吗？能。挪到右边。要证明这笔注。只是把钱放下，不算证明。要 size in，比着原注量过，才算证明。硬 12 加倍聪明吗？从概率上说不聪明，因为他可能爆牌，钱就没了。就像洗牌，你们必须宣布。黄卡出来的时候我们说什么？Last hand。你不是在要许可。你是在大声宣布。这种加倍叫 red flag，因为他有爆掉的可能。

videos.transcript_en: We have seven pink. How do we break down seven pink? Three, three, one. Love it. Three, three, one. Cutting cheques properly comes into everything we're doing. Even when we're closing games, we have to cut the cheques properly. For your audition, let's say you give a twenty-dollar blackjack. What does a twenty-dollar blackjack pay? Thirty. Thirty, right? It's the bet plus half. Twenty, and what's half of twenty? Ten. Twenty plus ten is thirty. So that pays thirty. If you say three and three, but you come out five and one, that's the correct amount of money, but the answer is wrong. You're on your audition. If you do this at the casino, they're going to stop you and make you do it right, and then correct you in front of the players. Cutting the cheques properly is crucial. Even though the amount is right, the answer is wrong. It's got to be three and three. So how much do we have? Seventeen fifty. Yes. These pink cheques are a pain. They're hard. You still have to look at them to count them. If you want to go quick: five, ten, fifteen, seventeen fifty, and then you put it back correctly. What I do is look at each layer. Each layer is five dollars. It's three high. Three times five is fifteen, plus two-fifty is seventeen fifty. However you do it, break the cheques down properly. I will agree with the seventeen fifty. I will say put it away. You don't have a full stack, but we go four and whatever is left over, three. The white: you bring this out. Partial on the outgoing, full on the incoming. We break whites down by five. How much do we have? Twenty-four. A lot of new dealers break these small stacks down. Don't do that. You can go up to five high. Anything under five, we're not going to break down. We can go five high if we need to. You think it has to be even? No. We can go up to five high. I agree with you: twenty-four. Put it away. Now we also have quarters. Twenty-five-cent quarters. Rolls of quarters are what you get from the bank. A roll is ten dollars. That's how they come to the table, in paper rolls. When you need to use it, break it open and give the paper to the floor. videos.transcript_en: I'm going to have you add it, because you need to practice adding. But in real life, supervisors do this. As a supervisor, I will add it up. You can't make marks up here. You have to do it in your head. Fifty and fifty is a dollar, so I carry one. I add six, thirteen, seventeen, eighteen. One, eight, thirteen, fourteen, plus two is sixteen. One, four, eleven, twelve. Thirteen. One, three, four, seven, eight. Nothing to carry. And then it's just three. Then I sign my name as supervisor, and I sign my badge number. Now I give this to you. I say, okay, now you can sign it. Take the time, real quick, just to check it. Just because I wear a suit does not mean I don't make mistakes. That's my wife — trust me, I make mistakes. Remember, I have your back. I don't want a write-up, so I am not only checking this for me. It takes seconds. You are not staring at it. It's a simple check of the slip: the twenty-seventh, flag check, pit zero, table one. Then the totals: twenty-two thousand. Eleven thousand three hundred. Three thousand seven hundred seventy-five. And the smaller figures, including seventeen fifty and twenty-four. Now, as a dealer, add it up. Just check the math. If you agree with everything on this paper, sign your name underneath mine with your badge number. The number on the badge you have now is an employee ID. It says who you are. Once you become a dealer, they give you another number. That is your badge number, and that is what you use to sign. Put the closer over the white and the red, and put the lid back on. You still wait. Stand here for your pit boss. He says take your lid off, set it down, and give me the closer. No one can reach into your rack. Nobody. Only you. Do you want other people's hands in the rack you are responsible for? No. If I need a count while you are dealing, I can use a pen. I cannot use my hands. No one uses their hands in your rack. He is not going to take the closer out of your hands. Set it on the table, and he will pick it up. He does not ask you questions. He checks it quickly. If he agrees, he puts his initials up top. When he gives it back, put it over the white and red again, put the lid on, and double-check. Clap, play your hands, and now you can lock off your game and go to scheduling. So that's how we close a game.

cues.en: Then I sign my name as supervisor, and I sign my badge number.

cues.en: Twenty-two thousand. Eleven thousand three hundred. Three thousand seven hundred seventy-five.

cues.en: The smaller figures include seventeen fifty and twenty-four.

cues.en: If you agree, sign your name underneath mine with your badge number.

cues.en: Put the closer over the white and the red, and put the lid back on.

cues.en: Then stand here and wait for your pit boss.

cues.en: He says take your lid off, set it down, and give me the closer.

cues.en: No one can reach into your rack. Nobody. Only you.
cues.zh: 谁都不能把手伸进你的筹码槽。谁都不行。只有你。

cues.en: If I need a count, I can use a pen. I cannot use my hands.

cues.en: He will not take it out of your hands. Set the closer on the table.

cues.en: He checks it quickly. If he agrees, he puts his initials up top.

cues.en: Clap, play your hands, and then you can lock off your game and go to scheduling.

Sixty, a space, sixty, and then the seven-fifty. You need to be able to tell the difference between your bet and the payout. This right here, size it in. This right here, total. If we were going to pay them all in red, there is no need to break it down. Just size it in. Not a problem. If the player asks for green, we can do that, but break that down. If we were paying green and red and the color is not changing, we do not need to break that red down. But if you ask for green right now, now we do have to break it down.
